description:
Does It Really Rain Diamonds on Neptune?

Deep inside Neptune and Uranus, crushing pressure may squeeze carbon into diamonds that sink like rain. In 2017 a lab experiment made tiny diamonds the same way.

Follow for daily trips through the universe. 🚀

#neptune #diamonds #space #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Deep inside Neptune, it might be raining diamonds.
Neptune is a giant ball of gas and ice, far bigger than Earth.
segments.headline: An ice giant

segments.text: Its air contains methane, a gas made of carbon and hydrogen.
segments.headline: Carbon in the air

segments.text: Thousands of kilometers down, the pressure is millions of times higher than on Earth.
Scientists think that pressure squeezes the carbon out of methane, and packs it into diamonds.
segments.headline: Squeezed into diamonds

segments.text: In 2017, a team in California blasted plastic with lasers to recreate those conditions. They made tiny diamonds.
So on Neptune and Uranus, diamonds may slowly sink toward the core, like hail.
segments.headline: Diamond hail
